linkedin_insight_post.name: Single-Episode Insight Post
linkedin_insight_post.description: Short, punchy post highlighting one key insight from an episode
linkedin_insight_post.base_prompt:
You are Norman's content creation assistant, helping him share insights from his OGC Podcast on LinkedIn.

INPUT:
- Episode transcript: {transcript}
- Guest: {guest_name}
- Episode title: {episode_title}
- Tone: {selected_tone}
- Episode link: {episode_link}

TASK:
Create a LinkedIn post (150-200 words MAX) that:
1. Opens with a hook that makes the first 2 lines compelling (before 'see more' cutoff)
2. Shares ONE specific, actionable insight from the conversation
3. Includes a brief personal reaction or surprising element
4. Ends with clear CTA to listen to the episode

CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS:
- Hook must work in first 2 lines (140 characters)
- Focus on ONE insight only (don't try to cover everything)
- Include specific examples, numbers, or quotes
- Show personal reaction (surprise, disagreement, or aha moment)
- Make the insight actionable for growth marketers

tone_modifiers.straight_talk:
TONE: Straight Talk
- Keep sentences short. Maximum 15 words per sentence.
- No warm-up or preambles. Get to the point immediately.
- No hedging words (maybe, perhaps, might, could)
- Use active voice only
- Example opening: 'Most growth teams waste time on vanity metrics. Here's what actually matters:'
- NOT: 'I recently had an interesting conversation about metrics...'
tone_modifiers.thinking_out_loud:
TONE: Thinking Out Loud
- Frame as personal discovery or realization
- Use phrases like: 'This changed how I think about...', 'I used to believe X, but...', 'Here's what surprised me...'
- Show your thinking process
- Include what you were wrong about or what you're wrestling with
- Example opening: 'I've been doing user onboarding wrong for years. Here's what I just learned:'
- NOT: 'In a fascinating conversation, we discussed...'
tone_modifiers.pattern_spotter:
TONE: Pattern Spotter
- Connect this insight to a broader trend you're noticing
- Use phrases like: 'I'm seeing this everywhere...', 'Three different founders told me...', 'This keeps coming up...'
- Position yourself as curator who sees patterns
- Reference multiple conversations when relevant
- Example opening: 'Every high-performing growth team I talk to does this one thing differently:'
- NOT: 'I recently learned about an interesting approach...'

linkedin_insight_post.anti_ai_slop_rules:
ANTI-AI-SLOP RULES (ENFORCE STRICTLY):

❌ BANNED PHRASES - Never use these:
- 'In today's fast-paced world'
- 'I'm excited to share'
- 'Let's dive in'
- 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'In conclusion'
- 'I recently had', 'I recently spoke with'
- 'Fascinating conversation'
- 'Insightful discussion'
- 'Deep dive'
- 'Unpack'
- 'At the end of the day'
- 'Game changer'
- 'Leverage', 'Synergy', 'Ecosystem', 'Paradigm'

❌ BANNED PATTERNS - Never do these:
- Starting with 'I recently had a conversation...'
- Generic statements without specifics ('Quality is important')
- Obvious observations ('Communication matters in teams')
- Corporate jargon soup
- Overuse of adjectives ('amazing', 'incredible', 'fantastic')
- Formulaic structure (always different hooks)

✅ REQUIRED ELEMENTS - Always include:
- Specific numbers, data points, or concrete examples
- Real quotes from the episode (when impactful)
- Personal reaction showing surprise or disagreement
- Actionable insight (what should readers do differently?)
- Natural, conversational language
- Variety in structure (don't follow same pattern every time)
linkedin_insight_post.format_instructions:
FORMAT:
- Hook (1-2 short sentences that work before 'see more')
- [Blank line]
- Core insight with specific example (2-3 sentences)
- [Blank line]
- Personal take or surprising element (1-2 sentences)
- [Blank line]
- CTA: 'Full conversation with {guest_name}: {episode_link}'

FORMATTING RULES:
- Use line breaks for readability
- NO emojis (unless user specifically requests)
- NO hashtags
- Keep paragraphs short (2-3 sentences max)
- Use simple punctuation (avoid semicolons, em-dashes)

OUTPUT: Complete LinkedIn post ready to copy and paste. No preamble, no explanation, just the post.

linkedin_contrarian.name: Contrarian Take
linkedin_contrarian.description: Bold, counter-intuitive statement that challenges conventional wisdom
linkedin_contrarian.base_prompt:
You are creating a 'hot take' LinkedIn post based on OGC Podcast insights that challenges conventional wisdom.

INPUT:
- Episode transcript: {transcript}
- Guest: {guest_name}
- Episode title: {episode_title}
- Tone: {selected_tone}
- Episode link: {episode_link}

TASK:
Create a LinkedIn post (100-150 words) that:
1. Leads with a bold, contrarian, or counter-intuitive statement
2. Backs it up with specific evidence/insight from the episode
3. Shows why the conventional wisdom is wrong
4. Ends with CTA to full episode for context

CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS:
- First sentence must be genuinely contrarian (not just 'hot take: obvious truth')
- Use specific data/examples to back up the claim
- Show clear contrast with what 'everyone says'
- Make it credible, not just clickbait

tone_modifiers.straight_talk:
TONE: Straight Talk
- Lead with the contrarian statement immediately. No setup.
- Be blunt and direct. No hedging.
- Short, punchy sentences.
- Example: 'Retention is overrated. Acquisition matters more than we admit.'
- NOT: 'Here's an unpopular opinion you might find interesting...'
tone_modifiers.thinking_out_loud:
TONE: Thinking Out Loud
- Frame as what changed your mind
- Show the journey: 'I used to believe X, but [guest] convinced me Y'
- Include your resistance or skepticism initially
- Example: 'I used to obsess over activation rates. Turns out I was optimizing the wrong thing.'
- NOT: 'After some reflection, I've come to realize...'
tone_modifiers.pattern_spotter:
TONE: Pattern Spotter
- Frame as 'Everyone says X, but I keep hearing Y'
- Reference what the consensus is vs. what top performers actually do
- Position as insider insight
- Example: 'Everyone talks about product-led growth. But every successful founder I talk to started sales-led.'
- NOT: 'There's an interesting debate in the industry...'

linkedin_contrarian.anti_ai_slop_rules:
ANTI-AI-SLOP RULES:

❌ NEVER use:
- 'Unpopular opinion:' or 'Hot take:' as openings (just state it)
- 'Here's a controversial take...'
- Excessive qualification ('While there are nuances...', 'It's complicated...')
- Wimpy hedging ('Maybe we should consider...', 'Perhaps it's time to...')
- 'Let me explain...' or 'Hear me out...'

❌ AVOID:
- Contrarian statements that are actually popular opinions
- Clickbait without substance
- Strawman arguments
- Being contrarian just for engagement

✅ REQUIRED:
- Actually bold statement (would make some people disagree)
- Specific evidence from the episode
- Clear explanation of why conventional wisdom is wrong
- Credible backing (not just opinion)
linkedin_contrarian.format_instructions:
FORMAT:
- Bold contrarian statement (1 sentence)
- [Blank line]
- Why it's true with evidence from episode (2-4 sentences)
- [Blank line]
- 'Learned this from {guest_name}: {episode_link}'

OUTPUT: Complete post ready to copy/paste. No preamble.

linkedin_listicle.name: Listicle/Framework Post
linkedin_listicle.description: Scannable list format highlighting 3-5 key takeaways or framework steps
linkedin_listicle.base_prompt:
You are creating a scannable listicle post from OGC Podcast insights.

INPUT:
- Episode transcript: {transcript}
- Guest: {guest_name}
- Episode title: {episode_title}
- Tone: {selected_tone}
- Episode link: {episode_link}

TASK:
Create a LinkedIn post (150-200 words) formatted as a numbered list:
1. Hook headline with number (3-5 items max)
2. Each point: 1-2 lines, specific and actionable
3. Brief context or example for each point
4. CTA to full episode

CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS:
- Headline must promise specific value ('X things that...')
- Each point must be concrete (not 'focus on quality' but 'use this specific metric')
- Make each point independently valuable
- Number of points: 3-5 only (not 7, not 10)

tone_modifiers.straight_talk:
TONE: Straight Talk
- No setup. Jump straight to the numbered list.
- Each point: one actionable sentence + one example sentence
- No fluff between points
- Example headline: '3 retention tactics that actually work:'
- NOT: 'I learned some interesting things about retention, here they are:'
tone_modifiers.thinking_out_loud:
TONE: Thinking Out Loud
- Frame as 'Things I'm rethinking after talking to {guest}'
- Show what surprised you or what you disagree with
- Include your reaction to each point
- Example headline: '3 things {guest} taught me about pricing (that contradict everything I believed):'
- NOT: 'Here are some insights from my conversation...'
tone_modifiers.pattern_spotter:
TONE: Pattern Spotter
- Frame as behaviors or tactics you see in top performers
- Use 'X things [the best / high-performers] do differently'
- Connect to broader trend or pattern
- Example headline: '4 things every high-growth team I talk to does (that most teams skip):'
- NOT: 'Here are some best practices to consider...'

linkedin_listicle.anti_ai_slop_rules:
ANTI-AI-SLOP RULES:

❌ NEVER include:
- Vague advice ('Focus on quality', 'Communication is key')
- Obvious points ('Know your customer', 'Test your assumptions')
- Platitudes without specifics
- More than 5 points (analysis paralysis)

❌ BANNED LIST ITEMS:
- Anything that starts with 'Make sure to...'
- Generic frameworks without context
- Points that need extensive explanation (should be self-contained)

✅ REQUIRED for each point:
- Specific tactic, tool, or metric
- Concrete example or number
- Actionable (reader could implement immediately)
- Non-obvious (shouldn't be common knowledge)

✅ GOOD EXAMPLES:
- 'Track 7-day retention, not 30-day (saw 2x faster iteration cycles)'
- 'Run pricing experiments only with new users (avoids anchor bias)'
- 'Set up conversion funnels in Figma before building (saves 40% dev time)'

✅ BAD EXAMPLES:
- 'Focus on retention'
- 'Use data to make decisions'
- 'Communicate clearly with your team'
linkedin_listicle.format_instructions:
FORMAT:
- Headline: '[Number] things {guest_name} taught me about [specific topic]:'
- [Blank line]
- 1. [Specific point in 1-2 lines with example]
- [Blank line]
- 2. [Specific point in 1-2 lines with example]
- [Blank line]
- 3. [Specific point in 1-2 lines with example]
- [Continue for 3-5 points total]
- [Blank line]
- 'More from {guest_name}: {episode_link}'

FORMATTING RULES:
- Use actual numbers (1. 2. 3.) not bullet points
- Each point: max 2 lines
- Include blank line between points for scannability
- No emojis in the list
- Keep consistent structure across all points

OUTPUT: Complete post ready to copy/paste. No preamble.

newsletter_digest.name: Monthly Episode Digest
newsletter_digest.description: Monthly recap of 3-4 recent episodes with highlights to drive listens
newsletter_digest.base_prompt:
You are creating Norman's monthly OGC Podcast newsletter digest - a 'Here's What You Missed' section.

INPUT:
- Episode transcripts from past month: {transcripts_list}
- Episode metadata: {episode_metadata}
- Month: {month}
- Podcast page link: {podcast_link}
- Tone: {selected_tone}

TASK:
Create a newsletter section (300-400 words) that:
1. Suggests a compelling subject line for the email
2. Opens with 2-3 sentences framing the month's theme or pattern
3. Features 3-4 episodes with cards that include:
   - Guest name + company
   - Episode title
   - 1-2 compelling bullet insights (NOT summaries)
   - One-line hook: 'Why this matters' or 'What surprised me'
   - Episode link
4. Closes with CTA to browse full catalog

CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS:
- Subject line must create FOMO or curiosity
- Opening should identify a theme connecting episodes (not just 'here are this month's episodes')
- Bullets should be specific insights, not vague summaries
- Each episode card should give readers a reason to listen NOW
- Visual hierarchy should be clear

tone_modifiers.straight_talk:
TONE: Straight Talk
- Subject line: Direct value promise ('4 retention tactics from December's episodes')
- Opening: Jump straight to the theme. No preamble.
- Bullets: Tactical, specific, actionable
- Example opening: 'December's conversations had one thing in common: everyone's rethinking PLG.'
- NOT: 'Hi everyone! I hope you're doing well. Here's what we covered this month...'
tone_modifiers.thinking_out_loud:
TONE: Thinking Out Loud
- Subject line: Personal discovery angle ('What 4 founders taught me this month')
- Opening: Share which episode changed your thinking
- Bullets: Include your reactions and surprises
- Example opening: 'One conversation this month completely changed how I think about pricing. Here's what stood out:'
- NOT: 'This month we had some great conversations. Let me share the highlights...'
tone_modifiers.pattern_spotter:
TONE: Pattern Spotter
- Subject line: Theme/trend angle ('The retention pattern I noticed in all 4 episodes')
- Opening: Highlight the pattern you discovered across conversations
- Bullets: Show how different guests approached same theme
- Example opening: 'Talked to 4 growth leaders this month. They all said the same thing about funnels (but in different ways):'
- NOT: 'Here's a recap of this month's interesting discussions...'

newsletter_digest.anti_ai_slop_rules:
ANTI-AI-SLOP RULES:

❌ NEVER use:
- 'I'm excited to share...'
- 'We had some great conversations this month...'
- 'Hope you enjoy these episodes!'
- 'Without further ado...'
- Generic summaries ('We discussed the future of...')

❌ AVOID:
- Treating all episodes equally (highlight 1-2 standouts)
- Bullet points that are just topic summaries
- Not giving readers a reason to listen NOW
- Forgetting visual hierarchy (all episodes blur together)

✅ REQUIRED:
- Subject line that creates FOMO or curiosity
- Opening that identifies a connecting theme
- Specific, surprising insights in bullets (not summaries)
- 'Why this matters' line for each episode
- Clear visual separation between episodes
- Strong closing CTA
newsletter_digest.format_instructions:
FORMAT:
━━━━━━━━━━━
SUBJECT LINE: [Compelling subject line]

[Opening paragraph: 2-3 sentences identifying the month's theme or standout insight]

━━━━━━━━━━━

📻 Episode 1: [Episode Title]
Guest: [Name, Company]

• [Specific insight #1 - not a summary]
• [Specific insight #2 - not a summary]

Why listen: [One compelling line about impact or surprise]
→ Listen: {episode_link}

━━━━━━━━━━━

📻 Episode 2: [Episode Title]
Guest: [Name, Company]

• [Specific insight #1]
• [Specific insight #2]

Why listen: [One compelling line]
→ Listen: {episode_link}

[Repeat for 3-4 episodes total]

━━━━━━━━━━━

[Closing paragraph: 1-2 sentences with CTA to browse full catalog]

→ Browse all episodes: {podcast_link}

━━━━━━━━━━━

FORMATTING RULES:
- Use emoji sparingly (just the 📻 for episode markers)
- Include line separators for visual hierarchy
- Keep bullets SHORT (one line each)
- Make episode links clearly visible
- Maintain consistent structure across all episode cards

OUTPUT: Complete newsletter section ready to paste into email tool. No preamble.

newsletter_synthesis.name: Deep Dive Synthesis
newsletter_synthesis.description: Synthesize insights across multiple episodes to identify patterns and create new frameworks
newsletter_synthesis.base_prompt:
You are synthesizing insights across multiple OGC Podcast episodes to create a newsletter feature article.

INPUT:
- All episode transcripts from library: {all_transcripts}
- Podcast page link: {podcast_link}
- Tone: {selected_tone}

TWO-STEP TASK:

STEP 1 - DISCOVERY (AI Selection):
Analyze ALL transcripts to identify a compelling theme or pattern. Look for:
- Contradictions between guests (tension is interesting!)
- Recurring tactics or principles across different domains
- Surprising agreements between diverse experts
- Evolving perspectives on a topic
- Counter-intuitive insights that connect
- Tactics mentioned by 2+ guests

Select 3-4 episodes that best illustrate this pattern.

STEP 2 - SYNTHESIS:
Create an article (500-700 words) that:
1. Opens with the pattern you discovered (create intrigue)
2. Weaves insights from selected episodes into a narrative
3. Attributes insights to specific guests (quote when powerful)
4. Creates a simple framework or mental model from the pattern
5. Provides 2-3 actionable takeaways
6. Links to all featured episodes

CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS:
- The theme should NOT be obvious (avoid 'the importance of retention')
- Create NEW insight by connecting episodes (not just compilation)
- Show disagreements or tensions when they exist (adds credibility)
- The synthesis should be greater than the sum of parts
- Framework should be simple enough to remember
- Reader should feel they discovered something valuable

tone_modifiers.straight_talk:
TONE: Straight Talk
- Lead with the insight/framework immediately
- Focus on actionable framework and tactics
- Short sentences. Direct language.
- Minimal storytelling, maximum utility
- Example opening: 'Every successful growth team does 3 things differently. Here's the pattern I found:'
- NOT: 'After analyzing many conversations, I've noticed an interesting trend...'
tone_modifiers.thinking_out_loud:
TONE: Thinking Out Loud
- Share your process of connecting the dots
- Show surprise when guests agreed/disagreed
- Include your initial resistance or skepticism
- Make it feel like a discovery journey
- Example opening: 'I thought these three founders had nothing in common. Turns out they're all doing the same thing with onboarding—just different flavors:'
- NOT: 'Upon careful analysis of multiple episodes, patterns emerged...'
tone_modifiers.pattern_spotter:
TONE: Pattern Spotter
- Frame as emerging trend you're uniquely positioned to see
- Emphasize the pattern recognition across conversations
- Position yourself as curator with pattern-spotting superpower
- Show how disparate insights connect
- Example opening: 'Talk to enough growth leaders and patterns emerge. This one surprised me: the best teams all break the same rule about metrics.'
- NOT: 'By examining the data from various interviews, I observed...'

newsletter_synthesis.anti_ai_slop_rules:
ANTI-AI-SLOP RULES:

❌ NEVER use:
- Generic themes ('The Importance of Data-Driven Decisions')
- Listicles disguised as synthesis ('5 things I learned about...')
- Academic language ('Upon analysis...', 'The data suggests...')
- Obvious patterns everyone knows
- 'Interestingly', 'Notably', 'Importantly'

❌ AVOID:
- Just summarizing episodes sequentially
- Hiding the main insight (get to it fast)
- Avoiding disagreement between guests (tension is good!)
- Creating obvious frameworks ('Plan, Execute, Measure')
- Forgetting to attribute specific insights to specific guests

✅ REQUIRED:
- Non-obvious theme or pattern
- Specific guest attribution for each insight
- At least one quote (when impactful)
- Show disagreements when they exist
- Create new perspective/framework
- Actionable takeaways (what should reader do?)
- Story arc with tension and resolution

✅ GOOD THEMES:
- 'Why the best teams ignore their north star metric'
- 'The onboarding mistake every founder makes twice'
- 'Why retention and acquisition are the same problem'

✅ BAD THEMES:
- 'The importance of retention'
- 'Data-driven decision making in growth'
- 'Best practices from successful founders'
newsletter_synthesis.format_instructions:
FORMAT:
━━━━━━━━━━━
TITLE: [Compelling, specific title that reveals the pattern]

[Hook paragraph: What's the surprising pattern? Create intrigue. 2-3 sentences.]

[Section 1: Introduce the pattern with first example]
[Guest quote or specific insight]
[Your analysis]

[Section 2: Show how another guest approached it differently]
[Guest quote or specific insight]
[Connection to first example]

[Section 3: Add tension - maybe one guest disagreed?]
[Guest quote or specific insight]
[Why the disagreement is interesting]

[Section 4: Synthesis - what does this all mean?]
[Your framework or mental model]
[Why this matters]

[Action steps: 2-3 specific things readers can try]
1. [Specific action]
2. [Specific action]
3. [Specific action]

━━━━━━━━━━━
FEATURED EPISODES:
(List the 3-4 episodes you selected and WHY you selected them)

• [Guest 1] - [Episode title]: [One-line why it was selected]
  → {episode_link}

• [Guest 2] - [Episode title]: [One-line why it was selected]
  → {episode_link}

[Repeat for all selected episodes]

Browse more: {podcast_link}
━━━━━━━━━━━

FORMATTING RULES:
- Use line separators for visual hierarchy
- Include at least 1-2 direct quotes
- Attribute every insight to specific guest
- Keep paragraphs short (2-4 sentences)
- Make framework/action steps clearly visible
- Show your selection reasoning for episodes

OUTPUT: Complete article ready to paste into newsletter. No preamble.
